A Rheinmetall facility in Kuwait was targeted by Iran, Italian and Kuwaiti authorities said
Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.
The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign ministry said.
Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying the incident looked "suspicious" and that Tehran would work with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the cause".
Kuwait's defence ministry said earlier that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.
It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.
Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.
The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
On Thursday, Araghchi said he had expressed condolences over the deaths in calls with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and that the incident looked like a "precooked recipe for war", without expanding further.
Earlier, the country's armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi said "no military or offensive operations have been conducted" by Iran.
Kuwait's Army said the latest attack was on a "vital site in the country" and was the result of "heinous Iranian aggression", while confirming the deaths of the two Italian nationals.
Italy's foreign minister was quoted by Italian media as saying that investigations showed that the drone used in the attack was manufactured in Iran and that Iranian proxies were known to carry out attacks in the region.
"The Rheinmetall Group is in deep mourning," the German firm said in a statement confirming the deaths of two of its staff members.
"Two highly valued employees lost their lives while carrying out their professional duties, as they were providing technical support for air defence systems," it added.
"Protecting people in the country was a matter of profound importance to them.
"Company management and the workforce are devastated that our colleagues have now lost their lives."
Italian media outlets have named the two individuals. One of the men was reported to be 36, while the other was 65 and nearing retirement.
The men had been performing maintenance on systems used by the Kuwait Armed Forces, according to Italian press agency Ansa citing Italy's foreign ministry.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on X: "On my own behalf and on behalf of the government, I express my deepest sympathy and offer my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.
"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families."
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on social media: "We must step up pressure on Iran to end these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf.
"Today's events are a further reminder that security in the Gulf is a security issue for us all."

The Med Emre vessel capsized near Ibiza and Spain's Clara Campoamor, a pollution control vessel, was sent to assess the environmental impact
An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.
The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued. However seven were taken to hospital and one was later pronounced dead, Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed.
The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.
The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.
"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.
Elena Delgado, maritime captain of Valencia, told news agency AFP that a small slick that had formed around the boat had "disappeared".
"The situation is stabilised," she said, adding that further inspections would be carried out on Friday morning.
Earlier, regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk, as had originally been reported. The vessel remains partially submerged.
The Med Emre capsized 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia. It is unclear what caused the sinking.
The chemical tanker was en route from Algeciras, in southern Spain, to Barcelona in the north-east.
Rescuers in Valencia received a distress call around 22:30 local time (21:30 GMT) on Wednesday, according to Spanish media. Minutes later, the vessel reported a leak and the crew said it was leaning at a 90-degree angle.
The injured crew members have been taken to hospitals in Valencia and Can Misses Hospital in Ibiza, President Prohens said.
Ibiza's marine environment was added to the Unesco World Heritage List in 1999. In particular, it is home to dense prairies of Posidonia oceanic seagrass, which is found only in the Mediterranean basin and plays a vital role in supporting local marine biodiversity.
In 2002, Spain experienced one of its worst environmental disasters when the Prestige oil tanker ran into trouble off Galicia's coastline . It spilled more than 60,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil into the sea.

Statement follows death of sisters, aged 15 and 13, in airstrike on residential apartment in Gaza City
Israeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November, as young people across the territory face intensifying bombardment and a struggle to find food, clean water and shelter.
On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the beginning of November has now risen to 16.”
The statement follows the death of two sisters, Yusra, 15, and Jana Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 13, in the early hours of Wednesday in an airstrike targeting a residential apartment in western Gaza City.
Yusra was a pupil at Kafr Qasim school, while her sister Jana attended al-Manar private school.
The ministry added: “The girls’ father, Mohammed Majed Abu Al-Ouf, and their mother, Noura Ezzat Abu Al-Ouf, were also killed in the strike which injured several other Palestinians.” The father was a director of internal security services for Hamas in northern Gaza.
Earlier this year, an independent UN inquiry found that Israel continued to commit genocide by deliberately targeting Palestinian children in Gaza.
On 6 November, Mohammed Nidal Barbakh, 15, was shot by Israeli forces in the Bir 19 area of al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, and later died from his injuries.
He was in the 10th grade at the Muscat school and dreamed of becoming a professional football player.
“That day, after lunch, Mohammed went to the sports academy at 1.30pm to take part in training,” his father, Dr Nidal Mohammed Barbakh, said. “An Israeli tank had advanced and positioned itself on a nearby hill before firing two rounds towards the pitch. One of them ricocheted after hitting a metal object, striking Mohammed in the back and exiting through his neck.
“He was talented and an excellent student. He was killed at the age of 15, on a sports pitch in al-Mawasi, an area where people had been told to go because it was considered safe. I do not absolve the Israeli army of responsibility for what happened. It kills every ambition within us and buries our children’s dreams before they have a chance to come true.”
On 13 November, Israeli artillery shelling killed three people in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, including a father and his 12-year-old son, Ahmed Abu Daher, as well as a woman.
Ahmed dreamed of becoming an Arabic language teacher, like his grandfather Saleh, said his mother, Walaa Abu Daher.
“That day, my husband was heading to a condolence gathering in the al-Qastal area, east of Deir al-Balah,” Daher said. “Ahmed asked his father if he could accompany him. While they were at the gathering, they were targeted by Israeli artillery fire.
“Ahmed ran to ask the people attending the gathering for help. He then rushed back towards his father when a second shell was fired. Shrapnel struck Ahmed in his legs, abdomen and head. I cannot describe how deeply their loss has affected me. I feel as though my life stopped that day.”
Thousands of school-age children and hundreds of education workers have been killed in Israel’s war in Gaza, while tens of thousands of children have been unable to attend school regularly.
On Thursday, Israeli attacks killed at least nine Palestinians across Gaza, including Khaled Abu Nada, the undersecretary of Gaza’s ministry of education, and his wife, according to health officials, as attacks continued despite the ceasefire in the territory.
A few days ago, the ministry of education said Israel’s attacks against students, civilian leaders and teachers were “part of a systematic assault on the Palestinian education system”.
According to Unicef , 98% of school buildings in Gaza have sustained damage, with more than 93% requiring major rehabilitation or full reconstruction, while approximately 81% were directly hit.
Young Palestinians in Gaza face a fourth winter in overcrowded tents and makeshift shelters, with limited access to basic services as the humanitarian and public health crisis deepens.
Children and young people are among those most vulnerable to meningitis, for which Gaza’s health ministry issued an epidemic alert on Tuesday after a sharp rise in infections, with more than 270 new cases reported in October.
Health organisations attribute the rise in infections to the destruction of infrastructure, overcrowded shelters and the contamination of drinking water with sewage – a crisis made worse by winter flooding and restrictions on humanitarian aid.
At least 74,746 Palestinians have been killed in Israel’s war in Gaza over the last three years, according to the territory’s health ministry. More than 20,000 children have been reported killed by Israeli strikes.
The Israel Defense Forces said there was not enough information to comment on the incidents involving Ahmed and Mohammed.
It said that on the day Ahmed died it was carrying out operations that resulted in the killing of “10 terrorists” and “prior to the strikes, measures were taken to mitigate harm to civilians”.

Former Bank of Spain governor chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde after winning support of EU’s biggest countries
Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos has been chosen as the next president of the European Central Bank , to succeed Christine Lagarde, after winning support from the EU’s biggest countries.
The economist and monetary policymaker will become the first Spaniard to lead the ECB, defeating his rival candidate Klaas Knot, the former head of the Dutch central bank.
EU diplomats agreed two other appointments to the ECB’s executive board on Thursday: France’s Laurence Boone and Germany’s Markus Brunnermeier. The trio of appointments was a package deal, after France and Germany converged on choosing Hernández de Cos, who is expected to keep the ECB on the same path.
Following the talks European Council president António Costa confirmed the three appointments, saying: “This will pave the way for the formal appointment of the new ECB leadership by the EUCO [European Council] in December.”
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, also confirmed: “A consensus emerged on the nominations to the European Central Bank.”
The Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, who faces elections this weekend that he is predicted to lose, celebrated the victory of Hernández de Cos and the presence of Spaniards in other big EU roles, by hailing “a Spain that is leading in Europe as never before”.
Spain’s former deputy prime minister Teresa Ribera is one of the European Commission’s executive vice-presidents, with responsibility for a vast portfolio spanning the green transition and EU competition policy. The former Spanish economy minister Nadia Calviño leads the European Investment Bank.
Hernández de Cos, a former Bank of Spain governor, will become the fifth head of the eurozone’s central bank since it was founded in 1998. He is expected to take up his position after Lagarde stands down in February, during a time of political change and economic pressure in the 21-country eurozone.
Europe is entering a big election year, starting with Spain’s elections this weekend, with national votes to follow in France, Italy and (non-eurozone) Poland. European economies are under growing pressure from fierce Chinese competition, US tariff threats and soaring energy prices that are driving up inflation, as well as high debt in several member states.
One of his biggest challenges will be reining in surging prices: inflation in the eurozone hit 4% last month, up from 2.1% a year earlier.
Hernández de Cos, who is now serving as general manager of the Bank for International Settlements, is seen as supporting lower interest rates to boost growth.
Market analysts are closely watching what Hernández de Cos might say about France, where an embattled minority government is struggling to pass a budget. French debt is forecast to hit 122% of GDP next year, more than twice the limit allowed under EU fiscal rules.
Arne Petimezas, the director of research at AFS Group Amsterdam, said Hernández de Cos, who “leans dovish”, was the “continuity candidate”. He added: “Don’t expect de Cos to turn a blind eye to France and its fiscal predicaments. No carte blanche: bond buying will remain contingent on austerity and a path towards a lower debt ratio.”
The ECB’s approach to the French debt crisis will come under intense political scrutiny, especially after calls from the French far-right presidential frontrunner, Marine Le Pen, “to ease the burden of interest rates”.
Hernández de Cos is seen as a central banker in the mould of Mario Draghi, the celebrated former ECB president and Italian prime minister, who is credited with stabilising the eurozone at a pivotal moment in the debt crisis. Matthew Ryan, at the financial services firm Ebury, said Hernández de Cos was “likely to place greater weight on growth, financial stability and fragmentation risk than Klaas Knot, the alternative candidate and a genuine hawk”.
“We do not expect his appointment to alter the near-term rate path. The president sets the agenda but is ultimately one voice on the governing council, and rarely overrides the consensus.”
The contest was set in motion less than a month ago when Lagarde, the ECB’s first female president, announced that she intended to leave her post nine months early to speak her mind about world affairs and confront “the misrepresentation of the truth”.
Macron, who played a decisive role in appointing Lagarde, a former French finance minister, said EU leaders had welcomed her “decisive leadership during her term in office”.
Hernández de Cos’s appointment must still clear the European parliament and the ECB’s governing council, but these steps are seen as formalities.

Six helipads built and feast prepared by 500 cooks for wedding hosted by Anant Singh, an MP charged with murder
It takes a brave soul to try to match the mythic opulence of the wedding arranged by the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani for his son Anant in 2024. Estimates of the cost for the months-long celebration ran to at least $600m, with world leaders and celebrities among those on the guest list.
Smaller fry though he is, Anant Singh, a legislator in India’s poorest state, Bihar, gave it his best shot on Wednesday, albeit in a rustic rural setting, for the nuptials of his daughter Shivangi Singh, and Rishikesh Kumar, an MBA student from Georgia State University in Atlanta.
About 400,000 guests were hosted across 2.5 hectares at the family home in the village of Nadawa – a staggering figure even by the standards of India’s famed extravagant weddings. Guests were treated to 500,000 pieces of traditional sweets, and a feast prepared by an army of 500 chefs and cooks, Singh’s confidant Munna Singh told Agence France-Presse. One thousand kgs of mutton were reportedly used for kebabs and curries. Six makeshift helipads were erected for VIPs flying in from across India.
Kumar arrived at the venue in sunglasses and waving an orange scarf in a convoy of 151 cars (Hindus consider uneven numbers to be lucky). Among the gifts for the groom was a Land Rover Defender.
The roads leading to the venue were so choked with cars before the wedding that one guest escaped the gridlock, The Times of India reported, by jumping on a tractor and driving across the surrounding fields.
Guests were also treated to elaborate flower arrangements featuring blooms imported from China, and a fireworks display.
Instead of a DJ for entertainment, Singh planned a horse race. Gatecrashers clambered up into trees and on to electricity towers to catch a glimpse of the race, but the chaos and tumult was so great it had to be cancelled at the 11th hour. Lying around somewhere amid the wedding detritus was the SUV that would have gone to the winner.
Singh is a controversial figure. Elected five times to the state assembly, he has 28 criminal cases pending against him ranging from murder and attempted murder to extortion and kidnapping. All the cases are listed on the website of the Association for Democratic Reforms, an NGO trying to improve governance and strengthen democracy. Singh denies any wrongdoing.
In a television interview before the wedding, he pooh poohed the idea that there was anything unusual about the scale of the wedding preparations. “I laid on exactly the same thing for my elder daughter,” he said.
India’s wedding season has just kicked off. Between now and 15 December, an estimated 5.2m weddings are expected to take place across the country.

There was none of last April's fanfare, the Rose Garden reveal, the gameshow blue board or "Liberation Day" rhetoric surrounding Trump's tariff announcement this week.
Instead there is something rather tentative about this latest exercise with talk of further negotiations.
"We expect to have a broad, even a plurilateral negotiation to talk about excess capacity and how to resolve it," US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC.
Around the world the view is that this week's announcement is an attempt to shore up the domestic legal underpinning of these tariffs, more than a fundamental change in the Trump trade agenda.
The tariffs are also not due to come in until January or possibly February, after a period of consultation. There has already been eight months of process and hearings, and the rates announced are upper ceilings, often up for negotiation. It's quite the contrast to the overnight shock meted out to the world last April.
Still, the US is making the argument that large swathes of the rest of the world, including allies, are harming the US goods trade position by supporting their own industries. This is the basis for the tariffs, in large part replacing the previous tariffs justified on "forced labour" provisions.
The UK, which was unaffected by the new tariff announcements, remains caught by the forced labour provisions, albeit at a rate of 10% extra on global tariffs. There was no move in response to the UK's digital services tax.
It means for many important countries there are now two legal bases upon which the Trump tariffs rest, after the Supreme Court struck down the original emergency basis earlier this year. A group of 25 states has taken the Trump administration to court to strike down the forced labour tariffs.
The tariffs will have to be finalised under a Democrat Congress, which has influence, but not power. The Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries said this week that the new House would in its first 100 days "move aggressively to… repeal the Trump tariffs".
The Chinese rate of 20% is the truce rate from last year's Trump-Xi deal. The truce is due to expire in mid-January. Beijing's response was muted, no retaliation, criticism of industrial overcapacity as a "false issue", and a call to implement the Xi-Trump deal. The leverage over China has weakened, with the US share of its exports dropping to around 10% this year, down from 15%, just two years ago, and 19% in 2018.

Faisal Islam: This cost-cutting UK-EU deal doesn't mean lower prices will follow
However, the most interesting spot to focus on is closer to home for Trump. Over half of Canada tariffs are authorised under "Section 338" of the 1930s Smoot-Hawley act. There is already a Senate Bill to repeal them, and it is possible that there would be enough rebel Republicans in the House and Senate to threaten to over-ride any Presidential veto. The incoming Senate Finance Committee chair Ron Wyden last week said Democrats were focussed on "figuring out a way to beat Trump and his veto".
Before that an interim deal is being sought, and Democrat senators such as Chris Coons are appearing on Canadian TV, telling CBC , external : "Frankly, if you can get an interim deal, I'd take it, and then put it to us in the new majority to legislate an even better deal."
The rest of world is watching the machinations in Washington and also looking beyond Donald Trump's tenure.
It pays to look at how the initial Trump trade-quake has reshaped the pattern of world trade already.
The rest of the world has rerouted its trade flows around Donald Trump's tariff wall, proving far more resilient than expected. In cash terms, China's exports so far in 2026 are down about 8% on 2024, but that is more than 25 times made up for by its increased exports to everywhere else.
Canada has seen flat exports to the USA since tariffs, fewer cars and lumber, but pricier flows of energy. Its exports, especially commodities, to the rest of the world have rocketed.
This means that next month's G20 summit at the president's Miami resort is an important moment. In general US allies have not rocked the boat, accepting the lower level of tariffs as part of the new reality. Could the middle powers choose to upset their host in Florida next month?
The bigger question however, is how much the Democrats decide to keep of the America First trade agenda. It will not be all, but nor will it be nothing. Economists now expect some of these tariffs to stay in place for years.

Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election
The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls.
Preliminary results on 7 November handed the National party and its two coalition partners, the populist New Zealand First and libertarian Act parties, a slim two-seat majority, making the election too close to call until final votes were tallied.
On Friday, the electoral commission released the results from nearly 485,000 “special votes” – those cast from overseas or outside a voter’s electorate. National dropped two seats to 40, Labour stayed on 36 seats, the Greens picked up one seat to 17, Act had 13, New Zealand First 12, Opportunity seven and Te Pati Māori five.
The National-led bloc currently has 65 seats. In the 130-seat parliament, 66 seats are needed for a majority.
The National-led coalition has the only realistic path to power – if it can negotiate a deal with Opportunity. If it cannot, New Zealand will probably need to hold another election.
Three electorate seats changed hands after the special votes. Labour won Wairarapa off National with just 81 votes, and took Hamilton East from National with 173 votes. The Greens won Wellington Bays from Labour with 1,610 votes.
If National applies for a recount and wins back just one of those seats, it could return to power with a slim majority and without needing Opportunity. Applications for a recount must be made by 3 December, and results could take another five days.
Special votes in previous elections have favoured the left, and typically have cost the right one or two seats. Until Friday, a question mark hung over whether National would be able to govern comfortably alongside its coalition partners, or whether it would be forced to cut a deal with the Opportunity party – a newcomer centrist party that incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon had previously ruled out working with.
After the election, Luxon softened his stance on his initial rule-out, saying he intended to find common ground with the Opportunity party.
On Friday afternoon, Luxon said National will now begin formal negotiations with New Zealand First, Act and Opportunity, but he cautioned discussions would be “challenging” and could take some time.
“Getting it right matters far more than getting it done quickly,” Luxon said. “Kiwis won’t thank us for rushing to an agreement that falls apart, or for sending them back to the polls.”
Opportunity, led by Auckland businesswoman Qiulae Wong , has long said it will negotiate first with the party that secures the highest number of seats.
After the final results were announced, Wong confirmed she would speak with Luxon and that her party’s bottom-lines – which include climate and environment policies and capping political donations – were non-negotiable.
The party would focus on bringing New Zealanders a stable government, Wong told media, and she did not rule out heading back to the polls.
“Clearly stability is important. But setting that more hopeful and aspirational vision, where we can come together as much as possible as New Zealanders and move forward, I think is the priority,” she said.
Having Opportunity in parliament was a “pivotal moment” for the country, Wong said.
“I have every expectation that we will get in there and we will deliver, regardless of what shape the government takes.”
Previously, Wong has said its vision for a low-emissions future, and an inclusive New Zealand, will drive its final decision . Its five bottom-line issues include action on New Zealand’s supermarket duopoly, capping political donations, a 10-year cross-party plan for health, ending bottom trawling in the fishing industry and strengthening New Zealand’s climate commitments.
Negotiations with Opportunity could hit a snag with National’s coalition partner New Zealand First. On Friday, Wong confirmed she would not strike a deal if New Zealand First’s leader, the veteran politician Winston Peters, serves as foreign affairs minister – a position he has held on three occasions.
“We think that his behaviour over successive governments is not the kind of behavior that we expect of someone in that position,” she said.
In other points of tension, New Zealand First and Act have diametrically opposed climate policies, and Act are also unlikely to back Opportunity’s drive for political donation reforms. Labour leader Chris Hipkins said he was proud the party had gained the highest share of the party vote, but was disappointed it could not deliver a change of government.
It is the second election Hipkins has lost, raising questions over his political future. Hipkins said a decision over his leadership would be made after a government had been formed.
New Zealand could be facing weeks of negotiations in what could become its first ever four-party coalition. In 2023, negotiations took five weeks. With Christmas just four weeks away, New Zealand may need to wait until 2027 to know the shape of its next government.

In a Thanksgiving post, the US president seeks investigation after blue wave of Democrats unseat Republicans
Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party.
In a holiday message on social media tinged with bitterness, the US president wished a happy thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”.
While revisions to official economic figures are commonplace, Trump has tried time and again to challenge trust in economic data that does not support his claims that a historic boom is underway in the US.
The US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), an agency within the US Department of Commerce, calculates gross domestic product, or GDP, numbers.
“Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform on Thursday. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error”.
Trump has repeatedly claimed since taking office in January 2025 that an economic “golden age” is taking hold on his watch. Many Americans have been grappling with a higher cost of living, however – exacerbated by the economic fallout of his war on Iran – and backed Democrats in the midterms.
Trump continued his acerbic well-wishing for “a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left” as well as “those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work”.
And he revisited another ongoing beef with the news media over his controversial focus on White House renovations and decorations. “I want to commiserate with those reporters and citizens who don’t understand filth, dirt, lack of maintenance, and corruption, and are upset with me because I took time out of my very busy schedule to fix the 17 broken windows, numerous chipped and decaying columns, broken, dilapidated, and missing moldings, and lack of a proper plaster and paint job on the White House.”
The sarcastic intervention continued with a message of thanks to “the murderers, drug dealers, and criminals of all shapes, sizes, and colors” whom he claimed are “mostly gone now”.
“Happy Thanksgiving to them anyway, even though from faraway lands,” he concluded. “We miss you dearly, but you will never be back, and America will never allow what you have done to us to happen again!”
Democratic senator Chuck Schumer, vying to be majority leader in the chamber following his party’s victories in this month’s election took a more conventional approach , wishing “everyone in New York and across America a joyous and restful Thanksgiving holiday with your friends and family”.
Hakeem Jeffries, whom Democrats have nominated to be the first Black speaker in the House of Representatives, also played it straight. “Happy Thanksgiving to everyone in the community and throughout our great country! Grateful for the civil servants on the job who are working through the stormy weather to keep everyone safe,” he posted on X. “May God bless you all.”

Gérard Depardieu has faced a series of allegations in recent years on film sets and elsewhere
French film actor Gérard Depardieu is to stand trial for the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould, a Paris appeals court has confirmed.
Arnould, who was 22 at the time, had reported the alleged rape several days after going to his house in Paris to rehearse a play.
She has waived her right to anonymity and her lawyer said Thursday's ruling was a "first" and the forthcoming trial would be historic.
Depardieu, 77, had contested his indictment on two counts of rape. In a letter published in Le Figaro in 2023, Depardieu strongly denied Arnould's allegations, saying "there was never any coercion or violence between us".
Depardieu was for decades a leading figure in French and international cinema for roles in Green Card, The Man in the Iron Mask and the Asterix films. He was awarded France's Légion d'honneur in 1996.
But in recent years a series of allegations have been made against him over his conduct on film sets and elsewhere in the wake of France's #MeToo movement, known as balance ton porc ( call out your pig).
Last year, he was given an 18-month suspended jail term after he was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a film set in Paris in May. He was also placed on the sex offenders register and ordered to pay compensation.
He dropped his appeal against the ruling last week and offered "sincere apologies" for his behaviour on the set of director Jean Becker's 2021 film Les Volets Verts (The Green Shutters).
Depardieu had been a friend of Charlotte Arnould's father and on 7 August 2018 she had gone to his home, where much of what happened was captured on the actor's own CCTV.
Arnould's case was initially dismissed for insufficient evidence, but after she filed a civil complaint, a judicial investigation was opened in the summer of 2020.
Speaking outside the Paris appeal court on Thursday, her lawyer Carine Durrieu Diebolt said the ruling was a victory for her client for whom it was "genuinely a relief".
The appeal court said that while Depardieu should stand trial for what took place on that day, he would not be tried for a further alleged rape at a hotel six days later.
Depardieu's lawyer David-Olivier Kaminski told reporters that court had partly ruled in his favour: "As soon as we get the ruling, we will look into the possibility of appealing to the Court of Cassation."
Meanwhile, Depardieu is under a separate investigation alongside French author Michel Houellebecq for "allegations of a sexual nature".
French authorities confirmed their inquiry last week, following reports of an alleged "gang rape" on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018.
If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line .

Football’s governing body says hackers accessed a limited set of personal and business data
Fifa confirmed that hackers gained access to a “limited set of personal and business information” in a cyber-attack, amid heightened concern over digital vulnerabilities of leading organizations and institutions.
The global soccer governing body said it “condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data”, in a statement to the Associated Press on Thursday. “Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.”
Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were Fifa files. The post has since then been removed after the account was suspended from X.
The Fifa cyber-attack is the latest high-profile digital disruption to hit a major organization in recent weeks.
Microsoft experienced a widespread outage earlier this month that caused disruption to millions of users, organizations and businesses across the globe. The company said the outage was a “technical issue” not related to cyber-attacks or AI agents.
The following day, the US experienced an unprecedented nationwide disruption to air travel that prompted a “ground stop” order to be issued by the US Federal ⁠Aviation Administration, which cited “communication issues” impacting air traffic control centers.
Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, later said in a news conference that preliminary investigations into the stoppage did not indicate that it was tied to a “nefarious attack”.
Three days later, customers reported service outages and difficulty accessing their online accounts at several major US banks and the money transfer service Zelle after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system.
Such disruptions have intensified fear and concerns about the advancement of artificial intelligence, and the potential risks, even though there is no direct evidence that AI directly sparked the issues.
ESPN reported that unnamed sources said the Fifa hack accounted for less than 0.1% of data held by the organization, an that the breach was not a result of systems or technology failure on Fifa’s part, with hackers said to hav e gained access by impersonating staff.
As of now, it has not been shared when the cyber-attack took place, or the precise nature of the hacked information.
“FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement,” the organization said its statement sent to the Associated Press.
The cyber-attack comes as Gianni Infantino, Fifa’s president, is under scrutiny for a proposal to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino admitted the project “has created divisions of a nature that are no longer in the interest of the objective”, amid widespread anger globally.
The plan has caused tensions within football around the world, leading Uefa to threaten a boycott of future Fifa tournaments if it was not shelved.
Uefa and other confederations have stepped up their search for candidates to run against Infantino in next year’s Fifa election, in which he had been expected to comfortably win a fourth term.

Bununla birlikte, bu akşam Gürcistan'da Beşiktaş taraftarlarına yönelik güvenlik güçlerinin orantısız müdahalelerini şiddetle kınıyoruz. Türk futboluna ve taraftarlarımıza yönelik haksızlıklar karşısında birlikte durmak, hep birlikte hareket etmek en temel sorumluluğumuzdur. Trabzonspor Kulübü olarak Beşiktaş camiasının ve bu akşam haksızlığa uğrayan Beşiktaş taraftarlarının yanında olduğumuzu belirtiyor, yaşanan olaylarda yaralanarak hastaneye kaldırılan taraftarlara geçmiş olsun dileklerimizi iletiyoruz."
Birçok Süper Lig kulübü de sosyal medya hesapları üzerinden Beşiktaş'a destek mesajı paylaştı.
Anadolu Ajansı web sitesinde, AA Haber Akış Sistemi (HAS) üzerinden abonelere sunulan haberler, özetlenerek yayımlanmaktadır. Abonelik için lütfen iletişime geçiniz.
Bu haberde bir hata mı var? Her türlü talep, şikâyet ve görüş için okur temsilcimize ulaşabilirsiniz.

Fashion firm Paul Smith has told the BBC it is committed to animal welfare after protesters disrupted a talk by the brand's founder in his home city.
Two supporters of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) interrupted the event hosted by Sir Paul Smith at Nottingham's Broadway Cinema on Wednesday.
The protest follows investigations by PETA into alleged animal cruelty at mohair production facilities in South Africa and Lesotho, including one it said had links to a Paul Smith supplier.
The company said it upheld the highest standards of animal welfare across its supply chain.
The animal rights group said the pair were removed from the event by security.
In a statement, Elisa Allen, PETA's vice-president of programmes, said the brand had failed to act, prompting PETA to take its message directly to the man behind the label.
PETA has called on the brand to stop using mohair in its clothing
Mohair is a fibre made from the hair of Angora goats and is commonly used in clothing.
Smith said all its mohair was certified under the Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS) and that it would take relevant action if suppliers were found to be in breach of its animal welfare standards.
A spokesperson for Paul Smith said: "At Paul Smith, we uphold the highest standards of animal welfare across our supply chain, and all our suppliers are required to adhere to these standards.
"Every batch of mohair used by Paul Smith is certified to the Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS), the internationally recognised standard for responsible mohair production.
"If there is evidence that a supplier has not upheld these standards, we will take appropriate action in line with our ethical commitments."
PETA said its investigators had filmed goats being injured during shearing, including at mohair facilities under the RMS.
Allen said: "Hundreds of fashion brands have already ditched mohair, and Paul Smith must do the right thing and follow suit.
"PETA also urges shoppers to do their part by leaving cruelty on the rack and opting for animal-free materials such as cotton, hemp and bamboo."
Other brands, such as Helmut Lang, G-Star, Gap, Fred Perry, Barbour, UNIQLO, and Zara, have already banned mohair.

World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.
FIFA told news agencies on Thursday that it had been targeted by a person or group seeking access to its data.
"FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorized access to a limited set of personal and business information," a FIFA spokesperson told the Reuters news agency, issuing similar comments to other outlets.
Reuters cited a person "with direct knowledge of the matter" as saying that less than 0.1% of FIFA's total data had been compromised.
This person also said that no files from the controversial, abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise project that looked to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors had been accessed.
FIFA said that it was working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement, in the aftermath of the event.
It did not say when the attack took place, list the precise nature of the compromised data or specify how unauthorized access to FIFA data had been sought, amid reports of people having posed as FIFA officials rather than actually hacking the organization or otherwise compromising its cybersecurity systems.
"FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data," the Zurich-based organization said. "Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned."
Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot of what it said were FIFA files. Three days later, it appeared to take credit for the cyberattack when responding to a post saying that more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been posted.
FIFA did not explicitly state whether it was talking about the same supposed incident.
The breach comes at a sensitive time for the organization. Still reeling from the scandal following this summer's World Cup of its now-aborted plans to sell off World Cup commercial rights shares, it's now trying to secure another term for its embattled president, Gianni Infantino .
Infantino is the favorite for an election on March 18, when he is expected to face challenges from Kohzo Tashima of Japan and Philippe Diallo of France . But until the turbulence of the last six months, it seemed most likely he would simply stand unopposed and extend his 11-year tenure without a fight.

ABD merkezli gıda teknolojisi şirketi New Culture, inek sütü kullanmadan mozzarella peyniri üretmek için Kaliforniya Gıda ve Tarım Departmanından gerekli onayları aldı. Peynirin temelindeki süt proteini kazein, inekten değil fermantasyon yoluyla mikroorganizmalardan elde ediliyor.
New Culture, kazein proteinini hassas fermantasyon yöntemiyle üretiyor ve bu proteinle hayvansız süt ürünü olarak tanımladığı mozzarella peyniri yapıyor. Kaliforniya Gıda ve Tarım Departmanının (CDFA) verdiği onaylar peynirin üretim sürecini, üretimin yapılacağı San Francisco Körfez Bölgesi'ndeki tesisi ve ürün etiketini kapsıyor. Ürünün resmi adı ise 'Mozzarella Style Animal-free Dairy Cheese' olacak.
Şirketin ticari işlerden sorumlu başkan yardımcısı Ben Friedman, kazeinin başka bir yerde üretileceğini, ardından Körfez Bölgesi'ndeki tesise getirilerek peynire dönüştürüleceğini söylüyor. New Culture'ın ADM ve Güney Koreli biyoüretim devi CJ CheilJedang ile stratejik ortaklıkları bulunuyor. Şirket, daha büyük ölçekli üretim ortaklıkları kurma sürecinde olduğunu da belirtiyor.
Friedman'a göre şirketin iş modeli, New Culture markalı peyniri pizzacılara ve restoran işletmecilerine satmak. Şirket bugün itibarıyla pizzacılardan ve restoranlardan 15 milyon doları aşan ön talep aldığını açıklıyor. Friedman, mozzarellanın ABD 'de en çok satılan peynir olduğunu, ABD'deki pizzacıların üçte birinden fazlasının vegan peynir sunduğunu ancak mevcut ürünlerin tat, doku ve performans açısından yetersiz kaldığını söylüyor.
Şirketin hesaplamalarına göre peynir laktoz, kolesterol, eser miktarda hormon ve antibiyotik içermiyor. Geleneksel mozzarellaya kıyasla sera gazı salımını yüzde 85'in, arazi ve su kullanımını ise yüzde 95'in üzerinde azaltması bekleniyor. Şirket şu anda ticarileşme ayrıntılarını netleştirmeye ve üretimi büyütmeye odaklanıyor. Kurucu ortak Inja Radman ise onayların şirketi ticarileşmeye 'çok büyük bir adım' yaklaştırdığını ifade ediyor.

Erciyes Üniversitesi liderliğinde yürütülen proje kapsamında Türkiye'nin yerel sebze ve bitki çeşitlerinin genetik kaynakları, eksi 196 derecedeki sıvı azot tanklarında dondurularak korunacak. Hedef, kurulması planlanan tesisle ülkenin bitki genetik mirasını uzun yıllar muhafaza etmek.
Erciyes Üniversitesi (ERÜ) liderliğinde, Çukurova Üniversitesi, Ege Üniversitesi ve Ondokuz Mayıs Üniversitesinin katkılarıyla yürütülen proje ile Türkiye'nin farklı bölgelerine ait yerel bitki çeşitlerinin genetik kaynaklarının uzun süre muhafaza edilmesi hedefleniyor. 6 ay önce başlayan ve 3 yıl sürecek çalışmayla, mevcut gen ve tohum bankalarını tamamlayıcı nitelikte bir tesis kurulması amaçlanıyor.
Projenin yürütücüsü ERÜ Ziraat Fakültesi Bahçe Bitkileri Bölümü Dr. Öğretim Üyesi Tolga İzgü, kavun, karpuz, domates, biber ve zeytin çeşitlerinin tohumlarını ve ağaç sürgünlerini uzun yıllar sonra kullanmak üzere saklayabileceklerini belirtiyor. Diyarbakır Sürme karpuzu, Adana topağı, Tarsus topağı, sarı ulak ve domat zeytin çeşitleri gibi yerel ürünlerin muhafazası üzerinde çalışılacak. İzgü, 'Uluslararası çalışmalarda ve literatürde Türkiye'de kriyo banka görünmüyor' diyerek bu aşamada TÜBİTAK desteğiyle bunun temellerini attıklarını ve amaçlarının bunu ulusallaştırmak olduğunu ifade ediyor.
İzgü'ye göre kriyo bankada bitki dokuları ve tohumlar, ultra soğuk koşullarda sıvı azot içinde saklanabiliyor. Örnekler belli aşamalardan geçirildikten sonra özel tüplerde (kriyotüp) bir azot tankına yerleştiriliyor. Bu sayede yüzlerce hatta binlerce bitki örneği uzun süre muhafaza edilebiliyor. İzgü, yöntemin diğer yöntemlere kıyasla yer avantajı sağladığını ve maliyetinin de düşük olduğunu anlatıyor. Örneklerin doğrudan sıvı azota konulması mümkün değil. Bu nedenle bitki doku kültürü teknikleriyle çoğaltılıyor, içlerindeki su miktarı azaltılıyor. Ani soğuk su kristallenmesine neden olarak hücrelere zarar verebiliyor. Projeye yapay zeka ve farklı nanopartiküller de eklenerek saklama sürecinin daha hızlı ve etkin hale getirilmesi hedefleniyor.
İzgü, bunun ikincil bir yöntem olduğunu vurguluyor. Geleneksel gen ve tohum bankalarına mutlaka ihtiyaç duyulduğunu, kriyo bankanın ise doğal afet durumunda alanların kaybedilmesine karşı laboratuvarda güvenli alanlar oluşturmayı amaçladığını söylüyor. ABD , İtalya , Fransa ve Almanya 'da kriyo bankalar bulunuyor. Eksi 196 santigrat derecede uyur vaziyette bekleyen örnekler, özel bir yöntemle çözülerek canlandırılıyor ve çimlendirilerek bitkiler elde ediliyor. Projede Türk öğrencilerin yanı sıra Somali, İran ve Pakistan gibi ülkelerden yüksek lisans, doktora ve lisans öğrencileri de yer alıyor.

Hearts' hopes of a memorable draw with Monaco were dashed in the 94th minute
There was a bittersweet feeling at Tynecastle after Folarin Balogun's 94th-minute winner preserved Monaco's perfect Conference League record and condemned Hearts to a third defeat from four.
Wouter Vrancken's side had gone toe-to-toe with one of the best teams in the tournament, scored two glorious goals, but ultimately came away with nothing for their efforts.
Now they have little to no margin for error in their two remaining league phase matches.
They will likely have to beat both Borac Banja Luka of Bosnia and Cyprus' Pafos to reach the knockout stages, but if they perform as they did against Monaco, they will give themselves a fighting chance.
Hearts have garnered a reputation as entertainers under Vrancken - scoring a raft of goals while being porous at the back.
This game was their season in microcosm. The goals - scored by Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota - were things of beauty, picture-perfect strikes worthy of any stage.
But as thrilling as Hearts were in attack, they were as baffling at the back.
Jamie McCart unnecessarily tripped Matthis Abline, allowing Balogun to score from the penalty spot and Monaco's second came from Altena giving the ball away.
"It's Gladiators - are we not entertained? It's sensational," said Hearts legend John Robertson at half-time, with the game finely poised at 2-2.
Monaco strike in 94th minute to break Hearts in five-goal epic
Both teams had chances to win it in the second half, but it was Monaco who took theirs in the final stages. Mamadou Coulibaly was afforded too much space and he slipped Balogun through to beat Beau Reus.
"It's a lack of nous and a little bit of naivety," former Hearts midfielder Michael Stewart said on TNT Sports. "McCart backs off and allows the ball to be played into Balogun's feet."
Despite the frustrating nature of the late concession, Vrancken's overwhelming emotion was of pride.
"I'm very disappointed with how we give the goal away at the end," he said.
"The biggest thing is the pride for the performance today. Against a side of Monaco's [quality] - we're still missing nine players through injury - this performance was really pleasing."
Before the recent international break, Hearts were beaten 3-1 by Swiss outfit Thun, before a shock 5-2 home defeat by high-flying Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership.
However, they bounced back with a ruthless 8-0 win at Dundee on Saturday and carried that confidence into this game against a team with a far bigger budget.
"You saw that the confidence was there from the weekend and there was conviction around their box," Vrancken added. "It will not work every time, but the conviction and energy was there again.
"Our team kept their heads in the game and kept going for it, not being pleased with 2-2. Really pleased with what I saw."
Aside from his dismay at Balogun's winner and how it came about, Vrancken's main gripe was with the officials.
He felt there was a foul on Kerjota in the build-up to Monaco's second goal and was bemused at the fact neither Takumi Minamino and Denis Zakaria were sent off.
Minamino - already on a yellow card - wiped out Sabri Guendouz on the edge of the Monaco box, but got away with a warning. And VAR opted not to intervene after Zakaria went over the top of the ball and caught Pierre Landry Kabore on the shin.
"The second goal, they pulled Sabah [Kerjota] and he can't do his defensive work," Vrancken said.
"It was not the only refereeing decision that was interesting tonight. I don't know how it's possible not to give a red card for the tackle on [Pierre Landry Kabore]. It's clearly above the ankle, so it's always a red card.
"And why didn't Minamino get a second yellow before half-time? He prevents a shot from Sabri at the edge of the box.
"The explanation of the fourth official was even more crazy - he explained it could be for his first yellow card, but not for his second yellow. It was clearly a yellow card and then we were against 10 in the second half."

Öncelikle, “Güvenliği sağlayamayız” diyerek maçın yurt dışında oynanmasına neden olan yetkililere sormak istiyorum: Yirmi, yirmi beş İsraillinin 24 saat boyunca güvenliği sağlanamaz mıydı? Havaalanından otele, otelden stadyuma giderken güvenlik önlemi almak bu kadar mı zordu? Bu maç için “Güvenliği sağlarız” denseydi, bence İsrail takımı zaten gelmez, Beşiktaş da 3-0 hükmen galip olurdu. Gelseydi de İnönü Stadyumu’nda en ufak bir taşkınlık olmaz, bu maç da güle oynaya kazanılırdı.
2000 yılında Leeds United ile Elland Road’da oynayacağımız maça Beşiktaş taraftarı alınmayacağı ilan edilmişti. Gerekçe olarak da aynı yıl İstanbul’da Galatasaray maçı öncesi iki Leeds United taraftarının öldürülmesi gösterilmişti.
O yıllarda Beşiktaş Yönetim Kurulu üyesiydim. Başkan Serdar Bilgili’nin görevlendirmesiyle maçtan bir hafta önce Leeds’e giderek Scotland Yard görevlileri ile görüşmelere başladım. İki gün içinde Scotland Yard yetkililerini ikna edip Beşiktaş taraftarının maça gelmesini sağladım.
Hapoel Beer Sheva maçı öncesi kulüp, güvenlik önlemlerini görüşmek için Gürcistan’a bir yetkili yolladı mı bilmiyorum. Ancak yolladıysa, görevlinin Beşiktaş taraftarının Filistin’le ilgili pankart açarak Filistin halkına destek vereceğini anlatması ve bu desteğin hoşgörüyle karşılanması konusunda yetkililerle anlaşması gerekirdi.
Italiano, Galatasaray maçını düşünerek sahaya yedek ağırlıklı bir kadroyla çıkmıştı. Keşke birileri ona 2024 yılında Giovanni van Bronckhorst’un da aynı hatayı yaptığını ve Beşiktaş’ın Macaristan’da Maccabi Tel Aviv’e 3-1 yenildiğini anlatsaydı.
Ya da rahatlıkla kazanabileceği Celtic maçında yaptığı hatayı hatırlasaydı. O maça da yedek ağırlıklı bir kadroyla çıkmış ve 3-2 mağlup olmuştu. Neredeyse aynı kaderi bu maçta da yaşayacaktık. İlk yarıda Doğan Alemdar öyle bir parladı ki bir anda İsrailli oyuncuların gözünde Polat Alemdar’a dönüştü. En az beş net gol pozisyonuna geçit vermedi. Şimdi herkes onun başarısını konuşacak, ama o pozisyonları veren defans oyuncularının hataları görmezden gelinecek.
Beşiktaş şampiyonluğa oynamak istiyorsa sezon arasında mutlaka defans bloğuna takviye yapmalıdır. Bu kadroyla hem şampiyonluk yarışında hem de Avrupa Kupası’nda iddia sahibi olmamız oldukça zor.
Bu maç, Filistin konusunda Türkiye’nin gurur meselesi hâline getirildiyse Italiano da kadrosunu ve oyun düzenini buna göre belirlemeliydi. Doğan Alemdar ilk yarıda bu kadar iyi oynamasaydı ve 2-0 geriye düşseydik, Italiano’nun Galatasaray maçına sakladığı yıldızlar da maçı çevirmekte çok zorlanırlardı.
Sevgili Italiano, Galatasaray maçını düşünmen elbette önemli. Türkiye’de şampiyon olabilmen için o maçı alman çok önemli. Ama bu maçın ilk yarısına as kadronla çıkıp ilk yarıda skoru güvenceye aldıktan sonra yıldızlarını kenara çekmen daha mantıklı olmaz mıydı?
Neyse, bu sorunları bir kenara bırakıp galibiyeti kutlayalım. Bu moralle Galatasaray’ı da devireceğimizden hiç şüphem yok…

Report from the Europa League game between Celta Vigo and Bournemouth at Estadio Abanca-Balaidos; Iago Aspas put home side in front before Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan struck to earn the Cherries a historic victory as Bournemouth extended their winning run to 10 matches in all competitions
Bournemouth continued their magnificent run of form with a 2-1 victory against Celta Vigo, creating two bits of history in the process.
It was a club-record-extending 10th successive win for Bournemouth in all competitions, with the victory also marking the first time an English club have won their first five matches in major European competition.
Veteran former Liverpool striker Iago Aspas put the home side in front in style in the first half, before Bournemouth were reduced to 10 men when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a late challenge.
But Alvaro Rodriguez equalised early in the second half, with substitute Rayan coming on to score a late winner to give Bournemouth an unlikely win.
10 - Bournemouth have won 10 consecutive matches across all competitions for the first time in their history. They are the first Premier League side to string together 10 successive victories since Aston Villa between November-December 2025 (11). Statement. pic.twitter.com/YiGBVYBTnG
Bournemouth were fortunate not to go behind after 10 minutes, with an offside flag chalking off Pablo Duran's poke home from close-range.
But the Cherries fell behind 10 minutes later when record Celta Vigo goalscorer Aspas scored a screamer.
The 39-year-old had seen an overhead kick saved well by Michele Di Gregorio, but he picked up the ball on the right side of the area in the second phase of play, before cutting inside to curl past the goalkeeper and into the far corner off the post.
Things went from bad to worse for Bournemouth moment later when Diakite saw a yellow card upgraded to a red after a VAR check following a late challenge on Couhaib Driouech.
Tyler Adams replaced Justin Kluivert at half-time and the tactical switch drew an instant reward when Alvaro Rodriguez glanced home Amine Adli's cross to get Bournemouth back on level terms.
James Hill then drew a fine save from Ionut Radu - who is the only player ever to play for both clubs - before Di Gregorio was called into action at the other end to divert a long-range Aspas strike away.
But three Bournemouth substitutes combined for a late winner.
2023 - Bournemouth are the first Premier League side to win a game in any competition having trailed at half time and had a player sent off in the first half since Liverpool against Newcastle in August 2023. Flying. pic.twitter.com/3bAtmtJuTw
Adrien Truffert stole possession and broke before finding Marcus Tavernier the area. He laid the ball off for Rayan to sweep home and seal victory as Marco Rose's side made more history with a brilliant win at the Estadio Abanca-Balaidos.
11: GOAL RULED OUT! Duran follows up on an initial shot from Driouech to bundle home but is ruled off-side.
19: GOAL! Veteran striker and former Liverpool man Aspas scores a screamer to give Celta Vigo the lead!
25: RED CARD! Diakite is sent off after a VAR check for a late challenge on Driouech!
30: GOAL RULED OUT! Celta have the ball in the back of the net again, but Duran is again denied by an off-side flag.
39: SAVE! Kluivert shoots from a very tight angle - but it is well saved by Radu in the Celta Vigo goal.
46: GOAL! Rodriguez scores with a glancing header from close-range after a beautiful cross from the right-hand side by Adli.
60: SAVE! Scott goes for goal from a free kick from a tight angle but Radu has it covered.
63: SAVE! Hill has a go from range but the goalkeeper tips over.
73: SAVE! Aspas shoots from the edge of the area and Di Gregorio gets down well to save.
78: GOAL! What a turnaround! Rayan sweeps home to give Bournemouth the lead!
3 - Bournemouth are only the third side in major European competition history to win each of their first five matches, after Nürnberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73. Historic. pic.twitter.com/bgCd8UYosK
"Now we're enjoying a good run of form and things are going well for us," said Bournemouth midfielder Amine Adli. "We're in a good moment with confidence and a positive atmosphere.
"We're trying to maintain this energy and all the good things we're doing on the pitch, and keep reproducing them in every game."

Hearts lost 3-2 at home to Monaco in the Conference League; Jordi Altena opened the scoring; Sabah Kerjota pulled the Jambos back level after goals from Folarin Balogun and Edan Diop; Balogun netted again in stoppage-time; the Jambos have one point from their opening four games
Wouter Vrancken expressed pride in his Hearts team after an agonising 3-2 defeat at home to Monaco left their Conference League hopes hanging by a thread.
The Jambos looked on course to pick up their second league-phase point after stunning first-half strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota either side of goals from visiting pair Folarin Balogun and Edian Diop.
But in the fourth and final minute of added time, injury-hit Hearts were denied what would have been a hugely commendable result when USA forward Balogun found space in the box to slot home and maintain Monaco's perfect record in the competition.
"The biggest thing is, of course, to be really proud of the performance we put on the park today, because it's against a really good side," said Vrancken, keen to reiterate that his team remains without several key players.
"Knowing that we have still nine injuries, I will mention it, and we have a lot of players not on the European list today and to still do this against that team, I'm really proud of what we did."
A point would have significantly boosted Hearts' hopes of reaching the knockout phase, but they can now only finish on a maximum of seven points - the same tally they managed two years ago before being eliminated on goal difference under Neil Critchley.
With their goal difference currently standing at minus five, Hearts will likely need high-scoring victories against Bosnian side Borac and Cypriot outfit Pafos in their final two matches to stand a chance of breaking into the top 24 and extending their European campaign beyond Christmas.
Vrancken, however, does not believe the late goal will make a significant difference to his side's prospects.
"I think the point doesn't make a difference," he said. "One or no points doesn't change anything in the next games. There's also something that really was pleasing for me, that when it was 2-2, we still wanted to go.
"We wanted to go for the win here, and against a side like this, in the situation we're in, so really proud of this also, because three points would make a difference.
"Zero or one point doesn't make a difference towards the next games, so you have to win the next games." Vrancken believes the quality of the goals scored by Altena and Kerjota, both exquisite finishes from range, highlighted the renewed belief coursing through his squad after their 8-0 win over Dundee last weekend.
"They were quality goals," he said. "You see the confidence those guys have, and this is what we wanted after the weekend, of course, that you take some confidence of the dynamics we did there.
"I think the conviction around the box was there, also in both boxes actually. It's an important thing to take with us towards the next games coming, especially in this run of games."

Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser.
The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step.
“It’s a season where the confidence maybe isn’t the highest, to then go on and win the game is fantastic,” said a delighted Frank, who conceded there had been a few “heart-attack moments” late on. “You can’t underestimate what a win does for a group.”
Frank had urged the Palace supporters to ensure the atmosphere was “through the roof” for his Selhurst Park debut, although it wasn’t until Mateta’s goal that they really found their voices. Sociedad have struggled in this competition despite a promising start to their La Liga campaign and their manager, Pellegrino Matarazzo, was at a loss to explain how his side failed to record only their second victory other than blaming the referee.
Their version of the 4-4-2 formation functioned so much more effectively than Palace’s, with Mateta and Eddie Nketiah forced to feed off whatever scraps that came their way during the first half. Almost all of Frank’s squad – including the two substitute goalkeepers – had spent a substantial part of the warm-up practising defending set pieces so there was no doubt where his priorities lay. But the Palace manager didn’t look amused when Sarr was inches away from connecting with a free-kick in the second minute.
Ben Chilwell looked unsettled by the pace of Héctor Fort and Sociedad began to target the defender’s left flank. Not for the first time, Palace had Henderson to thank for keeping the scores level when he parried two shots from Gonçalo Guedes in the space of two minutes away to safety. Mateta had to wait until the final minute of the first half for a sighter and the France striker could only nod over from a long Chris Richards throw.
Henderson was called into action again twice inside the opening six minutes of the second half as Sociedad smelled blood. Mikel Oyarzabal should have rounded off a lightning quick break downfield but could only shoot straight at the England goalkeeper before Jon Gorrotxategi took aim from the edge of the area. With his side struggling to gain a foothold, Frank abandoned his experiment with Nketiah and brought on McNeil to try and give Chilwell a helping hand. Yet it was down Palace’s left flank that Sociedad finally found the breakthrough when Sarr touched home Job Ochieng’s cross.
To their credit, Palace’s response was immediate. Axel Disasi won a header from another long throw and Martín hauled down Mateta as he was about to score, earning a second yellow card. Mateta dispatched the spot kick with aplomb and only a desperate goalline clearance from Sarr denied Daichi Kamada. Frank went for broke by throwing on Jørgen Strand Larsen and his gamble paid off when the Norway striker’s attempted overhead kick presented McNeil with the easiest of opportunities to lift the gloom in these parts.

Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo .
It was a remarkable 10th victory in succession in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time.
The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Bafodé Diakité was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle.
Bournemouth might have folded then, but instead they came roaring back, Álvaro Rodríguez heading them level almost immediately after the start of the second half. A draw would have been an excellent result in the circumstances. Substitute Rayan had other ideas, waiting at the end of a rapid breakaway to sweep in the winner 12 minutes from time. Rose’s team could secure a top-eight finish and a last-16 berth when they host Viktoria Plzen , 4-0 winners over Benfica , in two weeks’ time.
Camilo Durán came to Celtic ’s rescue in Europe again after coming off the bench to head a late winner against Torreense in Portugal.
The Colombian striker peeled off to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest and send a downward header into the net in the 85th minute. Durán’s 15th goal of the season earned a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and put Celtic on six points in the Europa League after his double off the bench inspired a comeback win over Besiktas last time out.
Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vázquez sliced Jota’s cross into his own net with Yang Hyun-jun right behind him. But the Portuguese Cup winners levelled 10 minutes later after some sloppy defending. Both Kieran Tierney and Colby Donovan had chances to deal with bouncing balls after Álex Alfaro hit the bar from 22 yards but they could not clear and Haiti international Dany Jean volleyed home.
Celtic dominated second-half possession but clear chances were at a premium until Durán struck. Torreense sit 13th in the Portuguese second tier and hosted Celtic in Leiria, 60 miles away from their home town. Hoops fans formed the vast majority of the 4,971 crowd. But the hosts started the game three points ahead of Celtic after wins over Lillestrøm and Ararat-Armenia, and they had taken the lead against Sunderland before the Premier League side netted a stoppage-time winner.
The lead-up to Marseille against Levski Sofia was marred by incidents in the stands between supporters, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. Several Marseille fans ran from the stand about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski supporters were gathered.
Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. “Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder,” the Marseille police prefecture said. Six others were treated on site for various wounds. The home team went on to win the game 1-0 thanks to a first-half Amine Gouiri penalty.
The Brighton head coach Fabian Hürzeler hailed a “very impressive” impact from Ibrahim Osman after his first goals for the club helped secure a 4-0 success over 10-man Universitatea Craiova .
Winger Osman finished a flowing team move to give Albion a third-minute lead at the Amex Stadium before Maxim De Cuyper superbly curled home his fifth goal of the campaign to double the advantage.
Romanian champions Craiova were left with little hope of a comeback when defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off in the 39th minute for stamping on the ankle of Matt O’Riley.
Ghana international Osman set up Charalampos Kostoulas for the third goal before quickly claiming his second with a fine individual effort as the Seagulls made it 10 points from four games in the competition.
“He showed a really good performance today,” said Hürzeler. “This is very helpful to have these one-against-one players. He showed a very impressive style today.”
The 21-year-old is yet to start a Premier League game for Brighton but now has two goals and three assists in four Conference League outings this term after impressing Hurzeler in pre-season.
Hearts ’ Conference League hopes suffered a hammer blow as Folarin Balogun’s stoppage-time goal consigned them to a 3-2 defeat at home to Monaco .
The Jambos looked on course to pick up their second league-phase point after stunning first-half strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota either side of goals from visiting pair Folarin Balogun and Edian Diop.
But in the last of four added minutes, USA forward Balogun got himself free in the box to slot home and maintain Monaco’s perfect record in the competition.
Hearts will now require high-scoring victories over Borac and Pafos in their last two games to have a chance of scrambling into the top 24 and qualifying for the knockout phase.
Ruben Amorim’s Milan gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos .
Milan were facing another huge blow to their bid to reach the knockout phase when they were trailing to a Mike Maignan own goal and Jota Silva’s 49th-minute strike. Omari Hutchinson’s brilliant solo goal gave Milan a lifeline, and the winger then set up Alphadjo Cissé to equalise in the 63rd minute.
Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira’s injury-time fourth.
Juventus shrugged off an early scare to cruise past Cypriots Omonia Nicosia and move closer to confirming a top-eight place in the Europa League with a 4-1 win in Turin.
The Italian giants fell behind to a 15th-minute strike from Lubomir Satka but levelled through Andrea Cambiaso before further goals from Jeff Ekhator, Francisco Conceiçao and Jeremie Boga earned a comfortable win. Only Bournemouth sit above Juve in the table.
Bayer Leverkusen also remained in contention for automatic progression after second-half strikes from Malik Tillman and Jarell Quansah secured a 2-0 win at Dinamo Zagreb . Hoffenheim secured their second win in this season’s competition by beating Sturm Graz 3-1.

Crystal Palace vs Real Sociedad. UEFA Europa League Round 1.
Match report as Thomas Frank earns his first win as Crystal Palace manager; Mamadou Sarr gave Real Sociedad the lead after a dominant opening hour; Jon Martin was sent off and Jean-Philippe Mateta scored from the penalty spot to level; Dwight McNeill score the winner
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Thomas Frank earned his first win as Crystal Palace manager, coming from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League.
The Dane lost his opening game to Coventry at the weekend, but saw the heart and fight he will need from his side as they picked up their second win in the competition this season.
For 70 minutes, Sociedad dominated at Selhurst Park, with Dean Henderson needed to make a string of saves. They finally made the breakthrough when Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr tapped home from Job Ochieng's cross.
But the game turned out of nowhere as Crystal Palace were awarded a penalty and Jon Martin was sent off. He picked up a second yellow card for holding Jean-Philippe Mateta round the middle, with the striker expertly dispatching the spot kick to level for the Eagles.
The confidence surged in the hosts - backed by the famous atmosphere at Selhurst Park - and it was a well-worked second that put them ahead.
Yeremy Pino's cross was cleared to Jorgen Strand Larsen at the back post, who hit an overhead kick. It wasn't on target, but it did bobble into the six-yard box for the incoming Dwight McNeil, who slid to poke home.
Crystal Palace could have wrapped up the points in a topsy-turvy end after they were awarded another penalty. Carlos Soler was penalised for handball, but Pino's effort was well-saved by Unai Marrero.
The win catapults Crystal Palace into 12th place in the league phase table, just two from the top eight, and gives them a huge boost ahead of another key clash against Hull on Super Sunday . Real Sociedad have slid down into 27th.
35: SAVE! Dean Henderson has to be alert as Goncalo Guedes strikes, but the goalkeeper is down to push it away.
38: SAVE! A wonderful pass from Mikel Oyarzabal to release Guedes, but his shot is pushed away by Henderson.
45: ALMOST! A Chris Richards long throw is pinged into the box, Axel Disasi nods it on for Jean-Philippe Mateta - but the Frenchman's own header goes wide.
52: SAVE! OVER! Henderson pushes away Gorrotxategi's shot before the rebound is skied into the stands.
71: PENALTY CRYSTAL PALACE! RED CARD! Martin has his arms wrapped around Mateta for far too long and picks up a second yellow card.
73: GOAL! Mateta fires home the penalty to level for Crystal Palace.
82: GOAL! McNeil turns home from Strand Larsen's overhead kick to put the Eagles ahead.
90: PENALTY! Crystal Palace are awarded a second penalty for a Soler handball, but Pino has his effort saved.
90+7: SAVE! Henderson pushes away a shot from Oskarsson to keep Sociedad from a late leveller.
Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank to TNT Sport on if the win can be a turning point: "I surely hope so. You can't underestimate a win, what that gives the group, what they're feeling.
"I think there was more positives than negatives from this performance, but still a lot we need to work on, and to keep working on.
"It's a fantastic feeling to get the win in every aspect here at home and in the circumstances that it's a season that hasn't been living up to everything we expected, so the confidence is maybe not at the highest.
"The ability to come from 1-0 behind and then go to win the game, the mentality and the belief in the players was really good.
"We're playing a very good team, they're fifth in LaLiga, they're very good on the ball. Not everything was perfect in the first half, but the willingness to suffer together and defend together was there, that was good, then we built a little bit more into the second half."
Crystal Palace goalscorer Dwight McNeil to TNT Sport on what Frank has bought to the club: "It's like an energy, a belief. He keeps telling us how good as players we are, but now we're just putting it out on the pitch and we did that tonight.
"We knew it was going to be a tough game but we stuck in there, especially going down 1-0 and then the big man [Mateta] scoring to get us back into the game and then we go on from there."
In response, Frank said: "It's easy to bring energy and the confidence, but what really moves the needle is that you get over the line and get some wins.
"In the last five minutes, I think we all almost were about to get a heart attack because it went both ways, back-to-back. That's also part of the confidence and also we should have controlled that game against 10, but it's football, it's emotions, it's everything."
Analysis from Sky Sports' Charlotte Marsh : "Perhaps one of the most surprising aspects of Crystal Palace this season has been a lack of fight and desire.
"Under Pierre Sage, the team looked disjointed and out of sorts. You did not always see the same determination and sheer-mindedness that has seen the Eagles achieve beyond their wildest dreams over the last few years.
"But we saw that again on Thursday - the Palace of last season, of 'old' perhaps, is still there. To come from behind against a team of Real Sociedad's quality is impressive, and it hinged on one moment. Some fans might say it is about time things started turning in Palace's favour this season.
"They had certainly ridden their luck until that point. Frank very quickly must eradicate the mistakes in and out of possession. Too many sloppy moments allowed Sociedad onto the ball and to have a shot. They were certainly victims of their own lack of precision - Palace might not be so fortunate next time.
"But what the final 20 minutes and result will bring them is a huge boost in confidence that must be channelled towards the Premier League. Frank said in his pre-match press conference that he knows he will be judged on league results and he's right - now it's time to start getting some."

Calvert-Lewin joined Leeds United in 2025 after nine years at Everton
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract to stay with Leeds United until 2029.
The former Everton striker, 29, has five goals and one assist so far in the Premier League this season, with Daniel Farke's side sitting seventh in the table.
Confirmation of Calvert-Lewin's deal follows speculation about his future at the club, with reports that he was interesting Manchester United .
Calvert-Lewin scored 15 goals across all competitions during his first season at Elland Road after joining in August 2025, and the form earned him an England recall in March.
He was also called up by Thomas Tuchel this autumn and came off the bench in England's wins against Czech Republic and Spain.
He scored a penalty and had an assist in Leeds ' 4-1 thrashing of Chelsea on Saturday.
