Geçtiğimiz günlerde bir davete katılan Melisa Aslı Pamuk, omuzlarını açıkta bırakan, pelerin detaylı ve yere kadar uzanan siyah bir elbise tercih etti. Sade ve zarif görünümünü altın renkli bir kolyeyle tamamlayan güzel oyuncunun kıyafeti, fiyatıyla da dikkat çekti. Pamuk'un davette giydiği siyah elbisenin 91 bin 224 TL'ye satışa sunulduğu iddia edildi.
Melisa Aslı Pamuk'un söz konusu davete katılmasının ardından özel hayatına ilişkin yeni bir iddia da ortaya atılmıştı. 35 yaşındaki oyuncunun ikinci kez anne olmaya hazırlandığı öne sürülmüştü. Hakkındaki hamilelik iddialarını yalanlamayan Pamuk'un ikinci kez anne olup olmayacağı ise henüz netlik kazanmadı.
Oyunculuk kariyerinin yanı sıra özel hayatıyla da dikkat çeken Melisa Aslı Pamuk, milli futbolcu Yusuf Yazıcı ile yaşadığı ilişkiyi uzun süre gözlerden uzak tutmuştu. Ünlü çift, Mayıs 2024'te Fransa'nın başkenti Paris'te düzenlenen sade bir nikah töreniyle dünyaevine girmişti. Evliliklerinin ardından bebek heyecanı yaşayan Pamuk ve Yazıcı, 29 Ocak 2025'te oğulları Mylan'ın dünyaya gelmesiyle ilk kez anne ve baba olmuştu.
Kariyerine henüz 14 yaşındayken modellik yaparak başlayan Melisa Aslı Pamuk, 2009 yılında Best Model of Turkey yarışmasına katıldı. Yarışmada "Gelecek Vadeden Model" seçilen Pamuk, iki yıl sonra önemli bir başarıya daha imza attı. 2011 yılında Miss Turkey yarışmasını kazanarak Türkiye güzeli seçilen Pamuk, aynı yıl Brezilya'da düzenlenen Miss Universe yarışmasında Türkiye'yi temsil etti.
Sadri Alışık Kültür Merkezi'nde oyunculuk eğitimi alan Melisa Aslı Pamuk, televizyon kariyerine "Yer Gök Aşk" dizisiyle başladı. Ardından "Kurt Seyit ve Şura", "Ulan İstanbul" ve "Her Sevda Bir Veda" gibi yapımlarda rol aldı.

Wesley Fofana played all 90 minutes of Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United on Saturday
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for a controversial interview he gave on YouTube.
Fofana has been criticised for comments he made in the interview with YouTuber Zach Nani in which he appeared to joke about his penalty miss in a Carabao Cup shootout defeat at Liverpool .
He did not have permission to hold the two-hour interview, which was aired after Chelsea 's humiliating 4-1 defeat at home to rivals Leeds on Saturday, but Alonso said the matter was now "closed".
"It was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, it was not right, the content," said the Blues boss, who was speaking before Friday's Premier League match at Nottingham Forest .
"We are here to take things seriously. He's said it will not be repeated. We don't want these kind of things and they won't be repeated."
Alonso refused to confirm whether Fofana had been punished by the club, but said "we have addressed that with him."
'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over
Fofana's comments followed criticism from fans of his performances this season, including in last weekend's humiliation at the hands of historic rivals Leeds .
But interviewer Nani defended Fofana against the backlash, saying: "People can clearly see he wasn't happy. He admits he didn't play well and says he needs to improve."
The interviewer also defended Fofana's explanation for putting himself forward to take a penalty against Liverpool , saying the defender believed it was his responsibility as one of the senior players on the pitch.
The 25-year-old France defender has often struggled for form and fitness since completing a £70m move from Leicester City in August 2022.
He has made 81 appearances for the club in four years, but has played nine times under new manager Alonso this season.
In that time Chelsea have struggled with defensive frailty, conceding 20 goals in their 11 Premier League games.
They are eighth in the table after falling to a third defeat in their last four league matches.

Camilo Duran's 15-goal haul this season has made him an invaluable player for a Celtic side fighting for European progression
It would be difficult for a football manager to muster up a higher compliment for one of his players - given he should know exactly how much he did cost - but Celtic boss Martin O'Neill was rightly effusive in his praise for Camilo Duran.
With 15 goals in 23 appearances, six assists, and another late European winner on Thursday, the Colombian was once again the main man for a struggling Celtic side.
His double against Besiktas breathed life into their Europa League campaign last time out, and his late leap to nod in the winner against Torreense kept it alive.
Duran, 24, started on the bench but was brought on with just over half an hour to go as O'Neill watched his side labour against a team currently 13th in the Portuguese second tier.
Celtic would still be searching for their first European win were it not for their summer arrival from Qarabag, whose goals have played a key part in keeping his team within touching distance of a play-off spot with three fixtures to play.
"He's taken on this mantle of being the man and he's been fantastic," said O'Neill, who started Duran on the bench. "We tried a similar approach against Besiktas.
"Sometimes by the time Duran gets subbed on, you could be behind. But I think that's the sign of a brilliant player, he'll do something.
"He's not a big guy but he's just a super footballer, a super, super footballer."
Duran's summer arrival was overshadowed when, just over a fortnight later, a club-record fee was paid to Bodo Glimt for another striker, Kasper Hogh.
While recent weeks have been dominated by debates over Duran or Hogh , the debate now seems settled, with the Colombian operating on a different level from his striking counterpart.
Anyone watching Celtic in Portugal would have watched Hogh find space a handful of times in the area, but repeatedly fail to find a team-mate or trouble the goalkeeper. Duran didn't need to be asked twice.
"I don't know how many touches he got, but he had the telling touch," James McFadden said on Sportsound post-match.
Duran's goals have also proved decisive in securing domestic points against Falkirk and Hibernian, and with Celtic just a point clear of Rangers, he is indeed invaluable.
Despite his late header giving the thousands of travelling Celtic fans a thrilling end to a relatively turgid game, the intervention is another significant moment in a season that is threatening to unravel if individual performances fail to continue papering over glaring deficiencies across the park.
If the lively Jota - who lasted 74 minutes - was not creating chances, tormenting full-backs or digging out enticing crosses in the first half, Celtic seemed without any real plan of attack.
Yang and Luke McCowan's involvements were limited at best, Hogh's chance to stake a claim was sub-par to be kind, and there was no driving force from the middle of the park to show some impetus.
Arithmetically, Celtic can still finish in any position in the Europa League table. But if they are to claim a playoff or automatic qualification spot, they will need Duran to remain in such a rich vein of form.

Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford
Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. Simon Burnton
When Leeds recruited Dominic Calvert-Lewin on a free transfer during the summer of 2025 it is fair to say many of their fans were underwhelmed. Now though the news that the England centre-forward has penned a contract extension at Elland Road is a cause for celebration in West Yorkshire. Calvert-Lewin had proved somewhat injury-prone at his former club, Everton, yet Daniel Farke evidently knew what he was doing. The newly robust 29-year-old has scored 18 goals in 46 Premier League appearances for Leeds, 17 arriving in the last 36 games. With Calvert-Lewin now having signed a new, improved deal extending until 2029, attention is turning to Farke’s own contract. The German’s current agreement expires next summer but renewal talks have been under way for some time and, for the moment at least, the normally open Leeds manager has turned coy. “I’ve fallen in love with the club,” said Farke ahead of his upwardly mobile team’s home meeting with Coventry. “But I’m not willing to speak about my future.” Louise Taylor
Mauricio Pochettino will send out his first Manchester United XI at Old Trafford on Saturday hoping Senne Lammens’ errors for the season are over. The fumble of a simple aerial ball late on at Sporting that allowed Luis Suárez to salvage a point on Wednesday was dismal from the goalkeeper despite his head coach’s protestations that the backline as a collective was at fault for allowing the opening. Karl Darlow, United’s second choice, has Premier League experience after a stint as Leeds’ first choice towards the end of last season but has played only 30 games in all divisions in the past three years. That means, probably, that Pochettino will retain Lammens but if more mistakes follow then the Wales international Darlow may be handed his chance. Jamie Jackson
Being forced from the field with “stud marks all the way down the back of his calf” after a clash with Tottenham’s Mohammed Kudus towards the end of last weekend’s match led to Leif Davis missing his first Premier League minutes of the season. It left Ipswich’s central defensive pairing of Issa Diop and Dara O’Shea as their only players to have been on the pitch for the entirety of the league campaign so far. O’Shea said this week of playing with Diop that “the more games we play with each other, obviously the better we’ll become as a pair”. They’re being given the best possible chance, even if Ipswich are yet to keep a clean sheet and have already conceded 22 goals, from an opposition xG of 21.82. Only the league’s bottom two have conceded a higher xG. More surprising is that Aston Villa have the next highest tally, with 18.56. Tuesday, when Villa lost 1-0 at Galatasaray , marked out a month since their last win. They have drawn three and scored in only two of their six outings. Ipswich may be just two points and two places outside the bottom three, but a win would put these teams level. SB
“We are having a great week,” Virgil van Dijk said after Liverpool followed up their 4-0 dismantling of Manchester United with a 3-0 win at Club Brugge that reinforced the strides being made by Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Andoni Iraola’s team overall. Liverpool’s week contrasts starkly with their local rivals. Everton suffered the heaviest defeat and produced arguably the worst performance of David Moyes’s second spell in charge on Monday when going down 4-0 at Brentford . James Tarkowski’s red card made no difference, so superior were Keith Andrews’s side from the start, but the absence of the Everton captain could be keenly felt on Sunday. Liverpool won the first Merseyside derby at Hill Dickinson Stadium last season from a 100th-minute corner, capitalising on disruption to Everton’s central defence when Jarrad Branthwaite went off injured. Without Tarkowski the hosts may be vulnerable again. Jake O’Brien could get his long-awaited chance to stake a claim as Branthwaite’s partner in the most demanding circumstances. Andy Hunter
Georginio Rutter offered an insight into the Fabian Hürzeler effect at Brighton this week. “He has changed the mentality of some of the players: he wants us to run and give 100% – we did that last season but not as hard as he wanted,” said the Frenchman. “Some new players have come in and given us a new vibe.” While the likes of Luka Vuskovic – who surpassed Rutter as Brighton’s record signing in the summer – and Chema Andrés have quickly established themselves as first choices, the 24-year-old forward who joined from Leeds in 2024 has fallen behind Greek teenager Charalampos Kostoulas since recovering from a foot injury. Rutter started in the defeat by Hull last week but missed the opportunity to score his first Premier League goal in 13 appearances despite some promising moments. He may have to make do with a place among the substitutes again when Newcastle visit on Sunday. “I want to play in every game,” said Rutter. “When I’m on the bench, I’m not happy. However, I know it is part of football and I will always give everything.” Ed Aarons
The bad news for Spurs fans is that their trip to Sunderland coincides with engineering work prompting the closure of the train line between King’s Cross and Peterborough. It means visiting supporters travelling by rail must head from St Pancras to Bedford before catching a rail replacement bus to Peterborough. The only feasible service departs London at 6.33am, arriving in Sunderland at 1.07pm and involves three changes. The return journey features four changes but, at six hours, is marginally swifter. At the time of writing the cheapest return ticket was £180.30. Such rail disruptions on Sundays are depressingly common and raise awkward questions about the country’s transport infrastructure outside the capital and, consequently, the UK’s suitability to host the men’s Euros in 2028 and the 2035 Women’s World Cup. More immediately, Spurs hope to capitalise on the injury-induced absence of Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey and Granit Xhaka while home fans are intrigued to see how Xhaka’s understudy, the immensely promising 20-year-old Jules Ahoka, fares in a central midfield duel with Sandro Tonali. Crystal Palace have announced plans to create a singing section at Selhurst Park for their Carabao Cup quarter-final against Sunderland next month in an attempt to make up for the absence of the Holmesdale Fanatics . Thomas Frank will need all the help he can get on Sunday against Hull and for the rest of the season if Palace are going to rouse themselves from the foot of the Premier League. Hadise makyajsız haliyle kamera karşısına geçerek güzellik sırlarını anlattı. Ünlü şarkıcının yüzündeki morluğa ilişkin açıklaması ve yaptırdığı işlemler dikkat çekti.
Konser vermek üzere Türkmenistan'a giden Hadise, sahneye çıkmadan önce otel odasında hazırlıklarını yaparken güzellik rutinine ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu. Yüzünde yalnızca nemlendirici bulunan 40 yaşındaki şarkıcı, sahne makyajının detaylarını anlatırken cilt bakımına verdiği önemden de söz etti. Makyajına başlamadan önce yüzündeki küçük bir morluğu gösteren Hadise, söz konusu izin hangi işlemden kaynaklandığını açıkladı.
Yüzündeki morluğun dolgu işleminden kaynaklanmadığını özellikle vurgulayan Hadise, söz konusu izin mezoterapi uygulamasının ardından oluştuğunu belirtti. İşlem sırasında canının biraz acıdığını da söyleyen şarkıcı, şu ifadeleri kullandı: "Şuramda bir morluk var, görüyorsunuz. Dolgu falan değil. Bu mezoterapinin izi diyelim. Burası biraz acıtmıştı çünkü."

Marco Rose replaced Andoni Iraola - who ended up at Liverpool - in the summer
Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after staging a 10-man fightback to join a select band of teams to win their first five European games.
The Cherries trailed 1-0 to Iago Aspas' goal at Celta Vigo, and then went down to 10 men midway through the first half when Bafode Diakite was sent off.
But second-half goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan gave the Cherries a 10th consecutive win in all competitions, extending their club record run.
Bournemouth are only the third side to win each of their first five European matches (excluding qualifiers and including the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup), after Nuremberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73.
They top this season's table as the only club to win five out of five - and are closing in on a top-eight spot, which would mean they skip a play-off round and go straight into the last 16.
Some fans have told the BBC they have already booked hotels in Frankfurt for the final on 26 May.
As supporters sang about reaching that game, midfielder Alex Scott was asked for his thoughts on TNT Sports.
"Of course that's our dream. When you grow up wanting to be a footballer you dream of winning trophies," Scott said.
"Where this club has come from to where it is now, full credit to everyone who has built it.
"For players, it's a dream to be on the pitch playing for this club. We have still got wins to get to qualify into the top eight, and from there all focus is on pushing forward and hopefully we can go on and win it."
The Cherries are in unprecedented times, with their biggest trophy to date being when they won the second-tier Championship in 2014-15.
In terms of cups, they won the 1983–84 Associate Members' Cup - which later became the EFL Trophy.
Head coach Marco Rose, who replaced Andoni Iraola in the summer, said: "It's always allowed to dream.
"If you get a competition like this you want to achieve the best possible thing. We know it's far away to go. Many games. Now it's about getting into the top eight to avoid more games and then we can see step by step."
As well as just winning their games, Bournemouth are firing in the goals. They have netted at least twice in each match during this 10-game winning run.
And they are the first side to score at least twice in each of their first five matches in Europe since Queens Park Rangers in 1976.
The win on Thursday was made even more impressive by the fact they contested 75% of the game with 10 men.
It came days after Manchester United seemed to implode after an early red card against Liverpool , losing 4-0.
Former England manager Glenn Hoddle said on TNT: "They have deserved this result. They've played beautifully with 10 men - probably as good as I've seen a team play defensively and with the ball.
"I've not seen a team go down to 10 men for so long and dictate a game and deserve to win the game. They were absolutely brilliant."
Cherries boss Rose told BBC Radio Solent: "What a team, what a spirit, what an energy.
"I said to Ty [Tyler Adams] sometimes it's not about tactics and formations and stuff like this. [David] Brooks did a great job when we got one player less - he played right defender like he played it for 10 years. We changed in the right moment. Everyone did his job on a really high level.
"We were just relentless and we never stopped to believe in this win and that's why big, big, big congratulations to the team.
"You feel if you're one player down that it's a difficult night, but to handle a difficult night like this, it just shows the character of the team and of the whole group."
The coach's belief in what they are doing filters through to the players.
Amine Adli, who set up the equaliser, told the BBC: "At half-time, everyone still believed we can turn the game in our way and this is what happened.
"Everyone was like 'guys we can make it, we have to believe. If we score the game can change.'"
Earlier this month, the attacking midfielder said he saw a lot of similarities to the Bayer Leverkusen team he was part of in 2023-24.
That is not a bad comparison, considering they went unbeaten to win the domestic double, as well as reaching the Europa League final.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal until the summer of 2029 at Leeds; the striker joined the club in 2025 from Everton; he has scored six goals in all competitions this season; his form earned him a recall to the England squad
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal at Leeds, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2029.
Sky Sports News has been reporting that he was expected to commit his future to the club, which has now been confirmed.
Calvert-Lewin joined Leeds on a free transfer in the summer of 2025 after leaving Everton. He scored 15 goals across all competitions last season, and has scored six this season. He scored in a 4-1 win against Chelsea on Saturday.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Since he joined Leeds, Calvert-Lewin is the highest-scoring Englishman in the Premier League (19) - three ahead of his next closest countrymen, Morgan Gibbs-White and Ollie Watkins.
His form for Leeds saw him return to the England set-up in March, and he also featured in the September/October and November squads. Calvert-Lewin was not selected for the World Cup.
Ao Tanaka is also close to signing a new contract with Leeds, Sky Sports News understands.
The midfielder is understood to have agreed terms on a deal that will keep him at Elland Road until 2029. The 28-year-old's current contract was due to expire in the summer of 2028.
Tanaka has grown to become a key figure in Daniel Farke's side this season, starting in nine of Leeds' 11 Premier League matches. They have lost just 10 of the 66 games Tanaka has started since then.
Calvert-Lewin follows in the footsteps of Ethan Ampadu, Joe Rodon, Jayden Bogle and Brenden Aaronson, who all signed new deals in the summer. Leeds are also reportedly set to trigger Lukas Nmecha's one-year extension.
Leeds are seventh in the Premier League, four points from the Champions League places. They face Coventry next in the league on Saturday.
Ahead of the weekend's match, Daniel Farke has refused to shed any more light on his own new contract talks. He signed a four-year contract when appointed in 2023 and that is set to expire at the end of the season.
He was reported to have parted company with his agent in October while reaching an agreement with Leeds in principle to extend his contract until 2029.
Farke said: "I'm the manager of Leeds United. I sign players. I don't sign managers. Since I've been here, I fell in love with the people here, and I fell in love with the club.
"And the only thing I care for is our supporters because they had to suffer really for such a long time. I want to bring success to them. I care for the players, I care for the staff and this is the way I work.
"I think this is also the reason I don't like to talk about my contract at all because I have to lead the people here.
"I'm a leader of men and women at this club and and no one wants a leader who talks about his future, about himself, or whatever. And this also not my style."

Report from the Europa League clash between Torreense and Celtic at Campo Manuel Marques; Javi Vazquez' own-goal put Celtic in front; Dany Jean levelled before the break; substitute Camilo Duran headed in a late winner for the Hoops; Martin O'Neill's side are up to 25th
Camilo Duran came off the bench to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive with a vital win against Torreense.
The Colombian striker peeled away to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest, guiding a downward header into the net in the 85th minute.
Duran's 15th goal of the season secured a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and moved Celtic on to six points in the Europa League. His latest decisive contribution follows a match-winning double off the bench in the Hoops' comeback victory over Besiktas last time out.
Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vazquez turned Jota's cross into his own net, with Hyun-jun Yang lurking behind him.
However, the Portuguese Cup winners hit back 10 minutes later after some hesitant defending from the visitors. Alex Alfaro rattled the crossbar with a 22-yard effort, but neither Kieran Tierney nor Colby Donovan could deal with the resulting loose balls, allowing Haiti international Dany Jean to volley home the equaliser.
Celtic dominated possession after the break but struggled to create clear-cut opportunities until Duran's late intervention secured all three points.
The Hoops' attention now turns to Hearts on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, as they look to remain top of the Scottish Premiership.
Their next Europa League match is away to Omonia Nicosia on December 10.
2: CLOSE! Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain sends in a corner, it's flicked on by Liam Scales but Hyun-jun Yang can't knock the ball in before it's cleared.

19: GOAL TORREENSE! Alex Alfaro's effort rattles the underside of the bar, Celtic fail to make a clearance and Dany Jean fires in the equaliser.
33: SAVE! Jota's powerful strike is pushed over the bar by Adriel.

61: CLOSE! Jean looks to squeeze in a shot at the near post, but it's just wide.

84: GOAL CELTIC! Camilo Duran rises at the back post to head in James Forrest's cross. Celtic are back ahead.
Jota looked back to his best despite not scoring or providing an assist.
In his first European appearance for Celtic since 2025, the winger was a pest for the Portuguese side until he was replaced by James Forrest.
He created chances with some brilliant crossing with one turned in by Vazquez for the opening goal.
He has been sensational since arriving in the summer and he saved Celtic again.
Once again, slack defending and individual errors proved costly, allowing Torreense to remain well in the game.
Record signing Kasper Hogh started, but once again did not score. He is lacking in confidence, but how long do you stick with a striker who is not putting the ball in the net?
"I'm just delighted to have won, it keeps us going if nothing else. We've got six points on the board and we've still a couple of games to go.
"From an almost impossible position, having lost the first three games, we've given ourselves some hope.
"Three points tonight were of vital importance. There's lots we can still do to improve our game."
Asked about Camilo Duran, he added: "He's just a magnificent footballer.
"15 goals and we're not into December, he's been flying. He's a terrific player, and that's two games he's come up big for us."
Celtic winger Jota speaking to TNT Sports after his first European appearance for almost two years:
"It was a long road and I did my maximum to be as fit as possible.
"Right now, it's all about enjoying life. No expectations, just be professional and having the responsibility of being a Celtic player.
"It wasn't easy. I think we just had to stick with our plan and in the end it worked out, that's the most important thing.
"We must believe [Celtic can qualify]. Every game is a different battle, we know what to do."

Jagiellonia Bialystok’s head coach, Adrian Siemieniec, claimed this trip to Wearside to face Premier League opposition represented one of the biggest highlights of a career in which he has already celebrated a Polish title.
His players did everything to guarantee it was not an anticlimax as they revelled in highlighting Sunderland’s struggles in front of goal courtesy of some intelligent defending. Along the way they also responded to falling behind with an almost immediate equaliser and forced the impressive Robin Roefs into the evening’s more taxing saves.
It leaves Régis Le Bris’ team 13th in the Europa League table before their trip to Milan in two weeks’ time. If the playoffs remain well within reach, Sunderland’s hopes of automatic progress to the knockout phase are fading and a smattering of boos greeted the final whistle.
“Frustrating game,” said Le Bris, who, with one eye on Sunday’s Premier League game against Spurs here, rotated his starting XI. “It was a well deserved point for the opponent.”
The eastern Polish city of Bialystok lies close to the Belarusian and Lithuanian borders but the arduous journey to north-east England was not responsible for the lack of Jagiellonia fans.
Instead visiting supporters were banned from making the trip by Uefa as punishment for misbehaviour at Levski Sofia earlier this season.
Although a few breached this suspension – and were duly expelled – their general absence contributed to a strangely flat atmosphere on a brutally cold Wearside night.
Although Sunderland began in dominant mode they struggled to undo Jagiellonia’s indefatigable defence. It would prove a recurring theme. Granted, Enzo Le Fée contributed some lovely touches and often looked the best player on view but Le Bris’ playmaker needed support and it seemed in scant supply. When Le Fée cued up Nilson Angulo a goal seemed inevitable but a splendid visiting block served as a reminder that Jagiellonia appeared determined to play in the spirit of their founders – soldiers from the 42nd infantry regiment of the Polish army.
At least Malick Fofana’s fragile confidence was boosted by a superbly calibrated left-foot shot that forced a stellar save from Slawomir Abramowicz. The Belgium winger has struggled since arriving from Lyon in a £30m summer deadline day move but here was a hint – albeit somewhat isolated – of the potential that led Sunderland to engage in an extraordinary transfer tug of war with Crystal Palace.
Unfortunately Omar Alderete’s struggles this season continued in an error-strewn performance. In mitigation perhaps the centre-half – excellent last season – was struggling with an injury as, shortly before half-time, he signalled to the bench that he needed to come off and was replaced by Luke O’Nien.
With the need to keep legs fresh for Spurs paramount, Le Bris also ­withdrew Noah Sadiki and Trai Hume at the interval, sending on Jules Ahoka and Thomas Meunier in their place. The newcomers were soon celebrating.
When Le Fée – who would soon join Sadiki and Hume on the sidelines – crossed incisively from the right Timur Tutierov was just onside and the young Ukrainian striker delighted in heading Sunderland in front from close range.
That lead did not last long. Errors on the part of Ahoka and then, most significantly, Reinildo’s panicked, failed attempted back-pass left Kamil Jozwiak free to round Roefs and sweep home an imperious shot.
Roefs then made an excellent save to deny Jozwiak a second goal after another mistake from the immensely promising yet deeply inexperienced Ahoka as Sunderland fans’ simmering disgruntlement became audible.
When Roefs intervened again late on there was a sense of calamity averted.

Your questions answered by Sky Sports News' James Savundra on Chelsea's season, with Blues having lost three of last four in Premier League; Wesley Fofana’s unauthorised interview, the absences of Danny Welbeck and Estevao, and January transfer plans all addressed
After Chelsea fell to back-to-back losses with a 4-1 humiliation by Leeds at Stamford Bridge last Saturday, Sky Sports News reporter James Savundra examines the latest developments at Stamford Bridge.
As well as suffering a third defeat in four Premier League games, Chelsea and manager Xabi Alonso also faced the added frustration of defender Wesley Fofana giving an unauthorised interview this week, in which he laughed off his penalty miss in last month's Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool and revealed he had contemplated retiring during his time at Stamford Bridge.
Here, Savundra addresses Fofana's future, Joao Pedro's injury, transfer plans and much more...
Jake: Is Fofana expected to face any disciplinary action for his impromptu interview? Some of the things said in that were unacceptable from a footballer, especially one involved in as much off-the-pitch controversy as him.
James says: Xabi Alonso addressed this at Thursday's press conference. Fofana has apologised following the interview. The matter has been dealt with internally and there are no suggestions that the defender is set to miss any matches.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Whether the club look to punish Fofana with a fine is not known at this stage. Alonso made clear that this will not be repeated. It's completely understandable to emphasise with Chelsea supporters. Fofana simply hasn't justified the £75m that Chelsea paid Leicester City.
Benny: Why is Fofana still being chosen when every single fan watching football can see how poor his form is?
James says: At the moment there is a lack of real alternative options. Xabi Alonso stood behind the Fofana-Colwill axis during Thursday's press conference despite their clear struggles dealing with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brian Brobbey.
Liam Delap will prove a similar physical threat tomorrow [Friday] with an added point to prove. Ultimately, Chelsea trimmed down their squad in the summer in light of no European football. Maxence Lacroix would be starting, possibly ahead of Fofana right now if he was fit.
Colwill has found things difficult this season having missed the majority of the last campaign. In hindsight, should Chelsea have sold Trevoh Chalobah? Perhaps it was time for the academy graduate to end his Chelsea chapter but he rarely let the side down.
You could feasibly play Josh Acheampong at centre-back. The youngster has been a shining light this season. Yet he looks comfortable on the right. Do you want to upset something which actually seems to be working. And if Acheampong moves to centre-back, then does Marco Palestra play as a right-back?
The Italian impressed in Serie A as a wing-back but with Chelsea opting largely for a flat back four, is Palestra defensively good enough to fulfil that role. Aaron Anselmino remains an option but hasn't played a minute for the club this season.
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso of Wesley Fofana: "We have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it wasn't the right moment. The content wasn't right. "We are here to take things seriously and he said it wouldn't be repeated. We know it's something we don't want and they are not going to be repeated."
Mikey: Will Chelsea sell and buy any defenders and strikers in January? I feel we need stronger defenders with a better aerial ability and maybe a more out and out No 9 to challenge Joao Pedro and give us something different.
James says: Chelsea will spend money in January if they believe it will help them achieve their target this season - qualifying for the Champions League. They were pleased with what they did in the summer but accept that the squad still requires investment.
It seems unlikely any defenders will be sold given the lack of current options. A loan move would seem to suit Aaron Anselmino given his lack of options. The winter window is a difficult one. There's a sense that Chelsea could benefit from signing a more experienced centre-back, considering the moves for Emi Martinez, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck in every other area of the pitch in the summer.
The club have shown a willingness to tweak their transfer model and sign players for the here and now, in addition to targeting players for the future. A striker would appear unlikely given the presence of Emmanuel Emegha and Danny Welbeck. It will be interesting to watch Emegha's development if given a run of games in the absence of Joao Pedro.
The fact that Xabi Alonso opted for a false nine in three matches prior to Leeds would suggest he believes there are shortcomings in both Emegha and Welbeck's games. It feels more likely that Chelsea will revisit the forward line next summer.
JD: How has Joao Pedro's injury affected how Chelsea has been playing as an overall team, and how has Xabi Alonso had to adapt to it?
James says: The stats are undeniable. Since the start of last season, Chelsea average 1.8 goals per game when Joao Pedro plays, compared to 0.6 when he doesn't. It's quite staggering the difference that the Brazilian seems to make.
Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers look far more potent when they are playing off him. Danny Welbeck initially started in his absence at Brentford. However, he had virtually no impact and appears to have fallen down the pecking order.
Playing Rogers or Pedro Neto as a false-nine has been experimented with but Chelsea have looked blunt without a focal point - though Emmanuel Emegha scored in his first Premier League start which was really encouraging.
Xabi Alonso doesn't tend to give much away but he has described Emegha as being a player with "special" qualities. There's clearly an adaptation period required and Emegha missed a lot of football last season due to injury.
He was also signed prior to Alonso's arrival so it was very much a club signing. Chelsea's season has been derailed by the absence of key players such as Reece James, Joao Pedro and Moises Caicedo.
Alonso needs his big players to step up to ensure they can cope with the casualties - albeit to really key players.
Adam: Why does Alonso not start Welbeck whilst Joao Pedro is injured? Given his experience?
James says: The treatment of Welbeck has been puzzling. He performed really well in the opening two Carabao Cup matches of the season but has featured sparingly since the Brentford defeat.
It was interesting to see how late he was brought on against Tottenham despite Chelsea's need to turn the tide. The 36-year-old (happy birthday today, Danny!) clearly cannot get around the pitch with the same intensity and speed he did when he broke through at Manchester United but that was obvious when he was signed.
Alonso has deflected when asked about Welbeck's lack of minutes but perhaps his inability to press with intensity is one of the main reasons behind him spending more time on the bench than on the pitch.
He's still got a brilliant goalscoring touch - as seen last season at Brighton. He may benefit from more opportunities during a busy December period.
Tim: Should Chelsea be starting Estevao more often? If not, then what should we do with him? Where could we send him on loan if we can't guarantee minutes?
James says: Estevao has only started twice this season - both times at home. He made a huge impact on the pitch and on the supporters when he started in the win against Manchester United. His lack of physical robustness and defensive acumen would appear to be why Xabi Alonso has used him so sparingly.
However, I don't think his lack of minutes is going to be sustainable long-term. There's an argument given Cole Palmer's drop off that Estevao should get an opportunity at No 10. Chelsea see Estevao as one of their "untouchable" players and they would be extrem…
